title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theatre on 1971-02-19
lineage: 7inch two track BBD reel w/ Dolby A @ 7 1/2  ips > PCM501ES @ 44.055 kHz > PCM501ES analog out > Fostex D5 @ 48 kHz (Dolby not decoded?) > WAV > Cool Edit Pro (filtering and sample rate conversion) > SHN

ai_review.summary: Clean soundboard capture of the Feb 19 1971 Port Chester show, highlighted by smoking Smokestack Lightning, an iconic Easy Wind and a tight China>Rider, with excellent audio fidelity.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as one of the cleanest of the Betty Board era – a crisp sound‑board source that requires only minor pitch tweaks. Musically the night shines with Pigpen’s powerhouse on Smokestack Lightning and Easy Wind, a sparkling China Cat > Rider, and strong early versions of Bird Song and Deal, though a few lyrical flubs and a brief cut in Bird Song keep it from being flawless.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is ~4.36/5, most comments are enthusiastic about both performance and sound quality; only a few moderate critiques exist.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clean Betty Board sound‑board capture; some versions show minor pitch drift and a short cut in Bird Song, but overall crisp with minimal noise.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set sparkles and closes with a smoking China>Rider; second set launches with high‑energy Bird Song debut and tight transitions, delivering strong Pigpen‑driven moments throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s solos are highlighted – soaring bends on Know You Rider, wailing leads on Bird Song, and a superb tone that many compare to Clarence White.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is described as melodic and supportive, often “bombing” under the band’s grooves.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir receives praise for his psychedelic‑blues guitar work and energetic fills that push the group forward.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is a focal point – driving the jams on Smokestack Lightning, Easy Wind and Good Lovin'.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is called “thunderous” and tightly locked; despite Mickey Hart’s recent departure, the rhythm section holds strong.
